title: Relative importance of bystander-witnessed status and bystander CPR for outcomes after out-of-hospital cardiac arrest: a registry-based cohort study
summary:
When a person experiences a sudden cardiac arrest outside a hospital, their chances of survival may depend on whether someone witnessed the event and whether people nearby started resuscitation before the emergency medical services arrived. However, the relative importance of these two factors remains unclear.
This study aims to investigate how witnessing a cardiac arrest and performing resuscitation by members of the public are associated with patient outcomes. Of particular interest is the comparison between cardiac arrests that were witnessed but where no bystander resuscitation was performed and cardiac arrests that were not witnessed but where bystander resuscitation was nevertheless provided.
The study will analyse existing, anonymised data from the German Resuscitation Registry. Adults and children will be analysed separately because of differences in their clinical and epidemiological characteristics. The main outcome is whether patients arrive at the hospital with their own circulation restored. Additional analyses will examine survival until hospital discharge.
No additional examinations or treatments will be performed.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients with emergency medical services-treated out-of-hospital cardiac arrest documented in the German Resuscitation Registry are eligible. Adult patients (≥18 years) and paediatric patients (>7 days to <18 years) will be analysed separately. The adult cohort includes cases from reference centres of the German Resuscitation Registry only. The paediatric cohort includes all eligible registry cases, irrespective of the reference status of the participating centre. All eligible cases from the predefined complete registry years will be considered.
Exclusion criteria:
Children aged ≤7 days and cases in which death was confirmed without an attempted resuscitation by emergency medical services will be excluded.
Additional exclusions from the primary analysis include EMS-witnessed cardiac arrests, arrests occurring in nursing homes or medical practices, missing information on witnessed status, bystander CPR or the primary outcome, and unresolved documentation inconsistencies. EMS-witnessed cardiac arrests will be included as a separate reference group in an additional analysis.
